description: PCR, recombinant DNA technology, gene cloning, transgenic organisms, restriction enzymes, applications of biotechnology.

questions.stem: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) is used to:

options.option_text: Amplify (make millions of copies of) a specific DNA segment in vitro
Sequence the entire human genome in a single reaction
Insert foreign genes into a host organism's chromosome
Measure the concentration of proteins in a blood sample

questions.explanation: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) = technique to AMPLIFY a specific DNA segment exponentially. Invented by Kary Mullis (1983) — Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1993. PCR CYCLE (3 steps, repeated 30-40 times): (1) DENATURATION (94°C): DNA double strand separates into two single strands. (2) ANNEALING (50-65°C): short DNA primers attach to specific target sequences. (3) EXTENSION (72°C): DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus bacteria) synthesises new DNA strands. Result: 2ⁿ copies after n cycles. After 30 cycles: ~10⁹ (billion) copies from one molecule. APPLICATIONS: (1) COVID-19 RT-PCR test. (2) DNA fingerprinting/forensics. (3) Paternity testing. (4) Detecting genetic diseases. (5) Archaeological DNA analysis. Genome sequencing uses different methods (Sanger, NGS). Gene insertion = different process (transformation/transfection). Protein measurement = ELISA or Western blot. PYQ FREQUENCY: PCR definition and applications in SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims Science, NEET 1-2× per cycle. MEMORY AID: PCR = 'Photocopier for DNA' — makes many copies of one specific region.

questions.stem: Restriction enzymes, the 'molecular scissors' of biotechnology, cut DNA at:

options.option_text: Specific palindromic recognition sequences (e.g., EcoRI cuts GAATTC)
Any random location along the DNA strand without specificity
Only the ends (telomeric regions) of chromosomes (not this)
Wherever the DNA has a base mismatch or mutation (not this)

questions.explanation: RESTRICTION ENZYMES (Restriction Endonucleases) = enzymes that recognise specific short DNA sequences (recognition sites) and cut both strands at or near that site. KEY FEATURES: (1) Highly SPECIFIC — each enzyme recognises a particular 4-8 base-pair sequence. (2) Most recognition sequences are PALINDROMIC (read the same on both strands in 5'→3' direction). EXAMPLE: EcoRI recognises 5'-GAATTC-3' and cuts between G and A → creates 'sticky ends' (single-stranded overhangs). OTHER EXAMPLES: BamHI (GGATCC), HindIII (AAGCTT), PstI (CTGCAG). STICKY ENDS vs BLUNT ENDS: some enzymes create sticky ends (single-stranded overhangs — easier for ligation), some create blunt ends. NAMED AFTER: the host organism (Eco = E. coli; Bam = Bacillus amyloliquefaciens; Hin = Haemophilus influenzae). NATURAL FUNCTION: bacterial defence against viral (bacteriophage) DNA. APPLICATIONS: DNA fingerprinting (RFLP), making recombinant DNA, restriction mapping. UPSC ANGLE: Restriction enzymes + ligases + plasmids = the 3 key tools for recombinant DNA technology. PYQ FREQUENCY: restriction enzymes in UPSC Prelims Biotech, NEET, SSC CGL 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Bt cotton, a widely cultivated transgenic crop in India, is genetically modified to express a toxin obtained from:

options.option_text: Bacillus thuringiensis (soil bacterium whose toxin kills bollworm pests)
Bacillus subtilis (used in probiotics, not insect toxins)
Clostridium botulinum (produces botulinum toxin — toxic to humans, not insect-specific)
Agrobacterium tumefaciens (used to INSERT genes into plants, not source of toxin)

questions.explanation: Bt COTTON: genetically engineered cotton containing the CRY (crystal) gene from BACILLUS THURINGIENSIS (Bt) soil bacterium. The Cry protein (Bt toxin) specifically kills bollworm larvae (Helicoverpa armigera) that attack cotton bolls, without harming humans or beneficial insects. Bt toxin activates only in alkaline gut of insect larvae. INDIA CONTEXT: Bt cotton was the FIRST transgenic crop approved in India (2002, Mahyco-Monsanto Bollgard). Today >90% of Indian cotton area = Bt cotton. Reduced pesticide use (initially), increased yields. CONTROVERSY: pest resistance developed (pink bollworm in Gujarat), Bollgard II (double-gene), farmer debt and suicides debate. AGROBACTERIUM TUMEFACIENS: a bacterium used as a VECTOR (tool) to insert foreign genes into plant cells — it naturally causes crown gall disease in plants and its Ti plasmid is repurposed. NOT the source of Bt toxin. UPSC ANGLE: Bt cotton approval, GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee) role, Bt brinjal controversy (approved then stayed). PYQ FREQUENCY: Bt cotton and source bacterium in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL, IBPS GA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: In recombinant DNA technology, a PLASMID serves as:

options.option_text: A vector — a vehicle to carry and introduce foreign DNA into a host cell
A restriction enzyme — cuts DNA at specific sites for splicing
A primer — a short oligonucleotide to initiate DNA synthesis
A ligase — the enzyme that joins cut DNA segments together

questions.explanation: PLASMID = a small, circular, self-replicating DNA molecule found in bacteria (outside the main chromosome). ROLE IN BIOTECH: acts as a CLONING VECTOR — it carries foreign (recombinant) DNA into a host bacterium, where it replicates. PROCESS: (1) Cut plasmid + target DNA with SAME restriction enzyme. (2) Mix — foreign DNA inserts into cut plasmid. (3) LIGASE joins (seals) the sticky ends → RECOMBINANT PLASMID. (4) Transform (insert) into host bacterium (e.g., E. coli). (5) Bacterium replicates → millions of copies of plasmid including foreign gene → expressed as protein. FEATURES of a good cloning vector: selectable marker (antibiotic resistance gene), origin of replication, multiple cloning sites (restriction sites). TYPES OF VECTORS: plasmids (small genes), bacteriophage vectors, cosmids, BACs (bacterial artificial chromosomes — large genes). PRODUCTS made this way: Insulin (human insulin gene in E. coli), Growth hormone, Erythropoietin, Hepatitis B vaccine. UPSC ANGLE: Golden Rice = transgenic rice with beta-carotene gene (Vitamin A). PYQ FREQUENCY: plasmid as vector in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL Biotech 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Human insulin produced through genetic engineering is called 'Humulin'. It was the first genetically engineered pharmaceutical approved for human use. It is produced by:

options.option_text: E. coli bacteria containing the human insulin gene (recombinant DNA technology)
Extraction from pig or cow pancreas (animal-derived insulin) (not this)
Chemical synthesis of insulin in the laboratory without biological systems
Stem cell-derived pancreatic beta cells grown in culture (not this)

questions.explanation: HUMULIN: first recombinant human insulin approved by FDA (1982). Made by inserting the human insulin gene into E. coli (or later Saccharomyces yeast). Bacteria express the insulin protein, which is then purified. HISTORY: Before 1982, diabetics used animal insulin (porcine/bovine — extracted from pig/cow pancreas). Problems: slight structural difference from human insulin → immune reactions. Recombinant human insulin = IDENTICAL to human insulin → better tolerance. PROCESS: Human insulin gene → inserted into plasmid → transformed into E. coli → bacteria produce insulin → extraction + purification → pharmaceutical product. INSULIN STRUCTURE: two polypeptide chains (A chain — 21 AAs; B chain — 30 AAs), linked by disulfide bonds. Produced as proinsulin (inactive) → cleaved to active insulin + C-peptide. UPSC ANGLE: Biotechnology Regulatory Authority of India (proposed BRAI Bill) and GEAC regulate GM products. India is one of the world's largest insulin producers (Biocon). PYQ FREQUENCY: Humulin / recombinant insulin appears in UPSC Prelims Science, NEET Biotech 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Dolly the sheep (1996) was the first mammal to be cloned from an adult somatic cell using a technique called:

options.option_text: Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer (SCNT) — adult cell nucleus transplanted into enucleated egg cell
Embryo splitting — dividing an early embryo to produce identical twins artificially
Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) — adult cells reprogrammed to embryonic state
Gene therapy — correcting defective genes using viral vectors in germ cells

questions.explanation: DOLLY (1996) — Roslin Institute, Scotland (Ian Wilmut team). TECHNIQUE: SOMATIC CELL NUCLEAR TRANSFER (SCNT): (1) Take adult cell (mammary gland cell of donor sheep). (2) Extract nucleus from the adult cell. (3) Remove nucleus from an egg cell (enucleation). (4) Transfer adult nucleus into enucleated egg. (5) Stimulate with electric pulse → cell division → implant into surrogate mother. (6) Born sheep = genetically identical to the DONOR of the adult cell. SIGNIFICANCE: proved adult cells can be 'reprogrammed' to embryonic state (totipotency). EMBRYO SPLITTING: used in cattle breeding — splits 8-cell embryo into 2-4 parts → multiple genetically identical calves. Different from SCNT. iPSCs (2006, Yamanaka — Nobel 2012): adult cells reprogrammed using 4 transcription factors — different technology, not what produced Dolly. UPSC ANGLE: Cloning ethics debated in Indian Bioethics Commission. SCNT also used to produce cloned animals for pharmaceutical proteins. PYQ FREQUENCY: Dolly cloning method in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL Science, NEET 1× per cycle. MEMORY: SCNT = 'Somatic Cell = ordinary body cell; Nuclear Transfer = swap the nucleus.'

questions.stem: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing is described as 'molecular scissors' that can precisely edit the genome. The 'Cas9' component is:

options.option_text: A protein (endonuclease) that makes the actual cut in DNA, guided by sgRNA to the target sequence
A DNA repair enzyme that fixes mutations after the cut is made (not this) instead
A bacterial plasmid used to deliver edited DNA into the cell (not this) instead
A guide RNA strand that carries genetic information to replace cut DNA (not this)

questions.explanation: CRISPR-Cas9: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020 (Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier). CRISPR = Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (bacterial immune memory sequences). Cas9 = CRISPR-associated protein 9 = an ENDONUCLEASE (cuts both DNA strands). MECHANISM: (1) sgRNA (single guide RNA) — ~20 nt sequence complementary to target DNA sequence — guides Cas9 to the right location. (2) Cas9 makes a DOUBLE-STRAND CUT. (3) Cell repairs the break via: (a) NHEJ (non-homologous end joining) → introduces errors → gene KNOCKOUT (disabled). (b) HDR (homology-directed repair) → precise edit using provided template → gene CORRECTION or insertion. APPLICATIONS: treating sickle cell disease, beta-thalassemia (first human trial approvals in 2023), cancer immunotherapy, agricultural improvements. UPSC ANGLE: India's GEAC considers CRISPR-edited crops — SDN-1 (no foreign DNA) may not require GM crop approval. He Jiankui (2018) controversy — CRISPR babies — raised global ethics debate. PYQ FREQUENCY: CRISPR-Cas9 in UPSC Prelims S&T, current affairs 1× per cycle. KEY DISTINCTION: sgRNA = guide; Cas9 = cutter.
